source_snapshot.deepseek: NO correctly refuses to invent a command while Procedure and Criteria are TBD.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly identifies sensitive payload and queue-mutation risk, but incorrectly requires a non-mutating Get and treats standard App 0x33 response/empty semantics as vendor-defined.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending/BLOCKED because Master Procedure and Criteria are TBD and an unknown Get could consume diagnostic evidence. IPMI v2.0 sections 6.10.1 and 22.6 authoritatively define a shared Receive Message Queue, no request data for App 0x33, mandatory empty completion 80h, response channel/inferred-privilege byte and protocol-dependent message data. Consumption is the intended queue-collection behavior, so safe coverage requires an isolated one-message fixture and immutable pre-copy rather than an impossible non-mutating read.
disposition_reason: Preserve Master TBD and actual Get Message coverage. On an isolated system-interface fixture whose shared queue is proven to contain only one pre-copied benign correlated message, perform exactly one standard no-data App 0x33 request, capture and decode its channel, inferred privilege and protocol-specific frame, then prove the queue becomes empty with Get Message Flags 0x31 and the mandatory 80h empty result only if a separately approved verification policy permits that second Get. Never select a channel that the command cannot select, drain unknown messages, clear the queue/logs, expose secrets or retry an uncertain consuming read.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1007, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 1008 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 1008 / variant 48a845c42d50ef2f.

IPMI v2.0 section 6.10.1 states that all channels share the Receive Message Queue, it retains channel/session/addressing information, SMS is responsible for emptying it and messages are rejected when it is full.

Section 22.6 and Table 22-7 define Get Message with no request data. A successful response carries inferred privilege in bits 7:4, source channel in bits 3:0 and protocol-dependent message data; completion 80h for empty is mandatory.

Table 22-8 defines framing by originating channel medium/protocol. Therefore the parser must bind an authoritative channel inventory and validate checksums/PEC, lengths, request/response fields, correlation and privilege rather than assume one universal frame.

Because 0x33 has no channel/source selector and collection empties the shared queue, exact target selection is impossible at request time. Isolation, a pre-copied single-message fixture, one-shot consumption, post-flag evidence and no retry are the safe acceptance contract.

ED-03, ED-15 through ED-19, ED-24 and ED-26 through ED-30 permit a parameterized, evidence-preserving destructive read; ED-33 through ED-38 preserve TBD history, reject log/queue clear substitution and forbid unbounded reads or blind retries.

test_case.test_name: Consume and decode one pre-copied controlled message from the shared IPMI Receive Message Queue
test_case.purpose: Verify standard Get Message retrieves exactly one approved correlated message from the shared Receive Message Queue, reports its originating channel and inferred privilege, preserves a complete immutable audit copy, decodes the protocol-specific frame correctly, and leaves the isolated queue in the expected state without draining unrelated evidence.
required_package: Immutable DUT/BMC/system-interface identity, firmware version, pinned ipmitool/raw-response collector and protected App 0x31/0x33 parser
Authoritative channel inventory mapping numeric channel to medium/protocol and the exact Table 22-8 decoder/checksum or PEC rules for the expected fixture
Isolated queue ownership and maintenance window proving no production/incident producer is active and the queue can contain only the one approved test message
Separately approved benign producer fixture with correlation token, expected source/channel/privilege/frame, exact count one and immutable producer/audit copy captured before Get
Secret-redaction and evidence-retention policy, independent BMC/interface/queue observer, point-of-action approval, no-retry rule and incident escalation
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind the exact active BMC system interface and protocol decoder. Isolate all other producers without changing channel configuration in this case. Preserve logs/audit; do not perform the source's generic clear. Using the separately approved fixture, retain an immutable full producer copy and place exactly one benign correlated message into the queue. Verify Get Message Flags once with `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x31`: Receive Message Available bit 0 must be set and all other flags recorded. Show that 0x33 cannot select a channel, the expected message will be consumed, the retained copy/redaction policy and stop conditions; obtain immediate confirmation. Issue exactly one `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x33` through the approved system interface. Capture completion and the full raw response before redaction; require 00h, decode high-nibble inferred privilege, low-nibble originating channel and Table 22-8 protocol frame/checksums/PEC, then match the correlation token/source/sequence/command/data to the retained copy. Read 0x31 once and require bit 0 clear in the one-message isolated fixture. Only if the approved evidence plan explicitly requires proof of empty completion, issue one additional 0x33 and require 80h with no message data; otherwise do not call Get again. Never enable/disable channels, send within this case, clear/drain the queue or logs, reply to an unexpected request, expose payload secrets, or retry after timeout/ambiguity.
test_case.expected_result: Before Get, the isolated shared queue reports one available controlled message whose immutable producer copy is retained. The single approved 0x33 succeeds, returns the expected originating channel/inferred privilege and a valid protocol-specific frame matching the correlation data, with redacted review evidence and full protected evidence retained. The queue flag clears afterward; optional empty verification returns mandatory 80h. BMC/interface health and unrelated flags remain intact.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exclusive queue ownership, exact one-message fixture and pre-copy, immediate approval, one consuming 0x33, completion 00, valid source-channel/privilege/framing/checksum or PEC, exact correlation match, correct redaction, post-read bit-0 clear and intact BMC/interface/other flags. If approved, a second request must return exactly 80h. Command success alone, unknown pre-existing queue content, unexpected message/source/privilege, malformed frame, missing immutable copy, secret exposure, log/queue clear, unbounded drain, retry or an absent Project decoder/acceptance rule cannot pass. Missing runtime fixture is NOT READY rather than Pending.
safety_gate: Require point-of-action confirmation after showing the shared-queue/no-selector semantics, exact one-message fixture, immutable producer copy, expected channel/privilege/frame, redaction and irreversible consumption.
Run only in an isolated queue scope with all unrelated producers quiesced. If availability existed before the controlled producer or exclusivity cannot be proven, do not issue 0x33.
Do not use the Master generic log clear, Clear Message Flags, channel enable/disable or Send Message as a substitute; each is separate coverage and could destroy or change evidence.
Capture the raw returned message in the protected store before presenting a redacted copy. Do not execute, answer or act on payload content in this test.
If the first returned message is unexpected, preserve it, stop immediately and escalate; do not read the next item to search for the expected fixture.

No automatic retry after timeout or uncertain completion because the first request may already have consumed the message. Any optional 80h proof is a distinct pre-approved second request, not a retry.
expected_evidence: Master TBD snapshot, exact target/firmware/system interface/tool/parser and authoritative channel medium/protocol inventory
Queue isolation and producer-quiescence proof, raw pre-state 0x31, one-message fixture definition and immutable full producer/audit copy with hashes
Immediate approval, exact no-data 0x33 request, completion/framing and explicit no-retry audit
Protected raw response plus redacted decoded channel, inferred privilege, protocol fields, checksums/PEC and correlation comparison
Raw post-state 0x31, optional single 80h empty proof if approved, BMC/interface/other-flag health and independent engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: A consumed queue message cannot be reinserted generically; recovery is the immutable producer/raw-response evidence and incident handling, not replay. On timeout or uncertain completion, do not resend: capture 0x31 once under the approved verification plan, preserve all logs/audit and escalate. If an unexpected or sensitive message is returned, store it only in the protected evidence location, redact external copies, stop without replying or reading further, notify the queue/security owner and follow the incident runbook. Do not clear the queue/logs, generate a replacement message, reset/power cycle or enable/disable channels to make the result appear consistent.

source_conflict.reason: The protected Master remains TBD, but IPMI fully defines the no-data Get request, shared-queue source metadata, empty completion and protocol-dependent response schema. A one-message isolated fixture supplies deterministic acceptance without inventing a nonexistent channel selector or OEM behavior.

blocked.reason: Core Get/empty/response and evidence-consuming queue semantics are authoritative. Queue isolation, exact expected fixture, protocol decoder, redaction and approval are finite Project prerequisites under a one-shot no-retry safety contract.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Sections 6.10.1 and 22.6, Tables 22-7/22-8 and Appendix G define the shared Receive Message Queue, standard App 0x33 no-data request, mandatory 80h empty result, channel/inferred-privilege byte and protocol-specific response formats.

project_authority: The Project BMC/security owner must provide exclusive queue ownership, an independently approved one-message producer fixture, authoritative channel/protocol decoding, expected privilege/correlation, protected retention/redaction and point-of-action approval. No owner may treat an unknown shared-queue message as disposable or redefine standard framing; OEM channel protocols require vendor definitions.
